$comment: Declared degradation contracts. Each one names an upstream, the fault to inject, and what the endpoint must still do. scripts/prove-brownout.mjs executes them against a live server and writes the verdicts to public/brownout.json, which /brownout renders. A contract whose fault never reached the code is reported as not_exercised, never as a pass: a green proof for a fallback nothing ran is worse than no proof at all.
summary: Every fallback below has been executed against a running server with the upstream it protects against genuinely broken.

contracts.title: The intel heatmap keeps its tiles when pump.fun throttles
contracts.why: pump.fun answers a burst with 429 far more often than it goes down, and the board is the whole page. The retry honours Retry-After and the last-good tier carries the tiles through what is left, so a throttle costs freshness rather than the page.

contracts.title: The market page keeps its fear and greed reading when alternative.me is down
contracts.why: A single keyless index feed. The page is assembled from several independent reads, so one of them failing must cost that one figure and nothing else.

contracts.title: The news archive still answers when its bucket does not
contracts.why: Archive data is immutable once written, which is what makes a remembered copy exactly as correct as a live one. With nothing ever cached the honest answer is a retryable 503, so both outcomes are accepted and the tier says which happened.

contracts.title: A token page still resolves when DexScreener is throttling
contracts.why: One keyless read used to decide whether a token exists at all, so a throttle made a live token read as not found. It now retries behind a breaker with a last-known-good payload, and a definitive miss is reserved for cases where a source actually spoke.
